page: Amazon Web Services m7i.4xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs, consisting of 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for tile and int8 operations. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates average performance across most workloads. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1909.39, while the multi-core score reaches 14645.49. Cryptographic capabilities are supported by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA extensions, reflected in a Passmark CPU encryption test score of 15072.68.

The DDR5 memory subsystem delivers a cached read-only small block bandwidth of 1181.52 GB/sec, which drops to 75.78 GB/sec for uncached large block reads. For language model workloads, the instance achieves a top-tier text generation speed of 333.79 tokens per second using a small 135M parameter model, though prompt processing for the same model remains in the average tier at 1845.47 tokens per second. Medium 7B parameter model inference runs at an average speed of 15.01 tokens per second for text generation.

Lacking local NVMe storage, this instance relies entirely on network-attached storage, which represents a tradeoff for workloads requiring high-IOPS local scratch space. However, with 64 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM and dedicated compute resources, it is structured for general-purpose workloads such as web serving, database operations, and software compilation. The hardware profile offers a balanced resource density, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for enterprise applications that require modern Intel instruction sets without the premium of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware.
description: Amazon Web Services m7i.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring an Intel Xeon 8488C processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 memory. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps, though it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Benchmark data places the instance in the average tier for most compute and memory tests, including a Passmark CPU score of 23157.79 and a Redis SET performance of 20.92 million operations per second. Notably, it achieves top-tier performance in text generation for small language models at 333.79 tokens/second. This instance is suited for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, and web serving where dedicated Intel compute resources are required without local storage dependencies.
